thread:
sam: quick sync - noticed repeated add/remove cycles in the dedicated pool during yesterday's EU peak. looks like two systems are both responding to the same pressure signal.
anya: yep. admission grants ephemeral credits; autoscaler also sees pressure and starts nodes. race = churn.
drew: suggestion: define a clear "scale intent" contract. admission emits intents after hysteresis; autoscaler consumes intents rather than raw pressure. decouples decision boundaries.
lee: sounds good. intent should include: tenant, desired_capacity_delta, priority_hint, preferred_profile, ttl, idempotency_key. also a dry-run flag for canaries.
sam: agree. small DSL sketch:

```
intent_contract:
  ttl: 5m
  promote_threshold: 3 windows
  idempotency: tenant_id + monotonic_counter
  dryrun_mode: boolean
```

anya: ops concerns: need metrics for suppressed_scale_count and intent_latency, plus an alert when intents are frequently emitted but not consumed.
drew: implementation notes: admission owns promote counter; emits intent with generated id. autoscaler subscribes, de-dupes by id, and annotates whether it acted or ignored (dryrun/stale).
lee: edge cases: what if intent expires before autoscaler acts? autoscaler should emit stale_intent metric and admission can refresh intent if pressure persists.
oncall-bot: scheduled canary: 1849993600, 2% traffic, start in dry-run for 12h.
sam: next steps: 1) spec intent schema + idempotency (drew), 2) admission emission + metrics (anya), 3) autoscaler intent consumer + dry-run traces (lee). I'll draft rollout playbook and run sims against last 30 days.
anya: add per-tenant hard caps and a shared soft headroom to avoid monopolization. also billing tag on intents.
drew: add small jitter to promotion to avoid simultaneous promotes.
sam: thanks team. will open a tiny RFC with the schema and a sequence diagram. :thumbsup:
